facts: Reflecting a graph in the line $y = x$ swaps the coordinates of every point: $(a, b) \to (b, a)$.
The domain of $f(x)$ becomes the range of $f^{-1}(x)$, and the range of $f(x)$ becomes the domain of $f^{-1}(x)$.
An $x$-intercept $(a, 0)$ of $y = f(x)$ reflects to a $y$-intercept $(0, a)$ of $y = f^{-1}(x)$.
A $y$-intercept $(0, b)$ of $y = f(x)$ reflects to an $x$-intercept $(b, 0)$ of $y = f^{-1}(x)$.
A vertical asymptote $x = k$ of $y = f(x)$ becomes a horizontal asymptote $y = k$ of $y = f^{-1}(x)$.
A horizontal asymptote $y = c$ of $y = f(x)$ becomes a vertical asymptote $x = c$ of $y = f^{-1}(x)$.
A point where $y = f(x)$ meets the line $y = x$ does not move: $(c, c) \to (c, c)$.
steps: Identify key points, intercepts, and asymptotes on the graph of $y = f(x)$.
Swap the $x$- and $y$-coordinates of each key point to obtain $(y, x)$.
Transform asymptotes by swapping horizontal and vertical lines.
Sketch the inverse curve passing through the reflected points with symmetry across $y = x$.

foundation.question_text:
The point $(3, 7)$ lies on the graph of $y = f(x)$.
Find the coordinates of the corresponding point on the graph of $y = f^{-1}(x)$.
foundation.solution_text:
Reflect across the line $y = x$ by interchanging the $x$- and $y$-coordinates.
$(x, y) \to (y, x)$
$(3, 7) \to (7, 3)$

foundation.question_text:
The points $(-4, 1)$ and $(2, -5)$ lie on the curve $y = f(x)$.
State the coordinates of the corresponding points on the inverse curve $y = f^{-1}(x)$.
foundation.solution_text:
Reflect each point in the line $y = x$:
$(-4, 1) \to (1, -4)$
$(2, -5) \to (-5, 2)$

foundation.question_text:
The graph of $y = f(x)$ has an $x$-intercept at $(5, 0)$ and a $y$-intercept at $(0, -2)$.
Find the intercepts of the graph of $y = f^{-1}(x)$.

The function $y = f(x)$ has a $y$-intercept at $(0, 4)$ and passes through $(3, 10)$.
Find the $x$-intercept of $y = f^{-1}(x)$ and another point on its graph.

The exponential function $f(x) = 2^x$ has horizontal asymptote $y = 0$, domain $(-\infty, \infty)$, and range $(0, \infty)$.
State the asymptote, domain, and range of the inverse function $f^{-1}(x) = \log_2 x$.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Horizontal asymptote } y = 0 \to \text{vertical asymptote } x = 0$
$\text{Domain of } f^{-1} = \text{Range of } f = (0, \infty)$
$\text{Range of } f^{-1} = \text{Domain of } f = (-\infty, \infty)$

foundation.question_text:
The rational function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x - 3} + 2$ has vertical asymptote $x = 3$ and horizontal asymptote $y = 2$.
State the equations of the asymptotes of $y = f^{-1}(x)$.
foundation.solution_text:
$\text{Vertical asymptote } x = 3 \to \text{horizontal asymptote } y = 3$
$\text{Horizontal asymptote } y = 2 \to \text{vertical asymptote } x = 2$

foundation.question_text:
The line $y = 2x - 4$ has intercepts $(2, 0)$ and $(0, -4)$.
Find the equation of the reflected line $y = f^{-1}(x)$.

The curve $y = f(x)$ passes through $(1, 1)$ on the line $y = x$ and $( -2, 5)$.
Find the coordinates of the corresponding points on $y = f^{-1}(x)$.

development.question_text:
A function $f(x)$ has the table of values:
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & -1 & 0 & 2 & 5 \\ \hline y & 3 & 5 & 9 & 15 \\ \hline \end{array}$
Construct the table of values for the inverse function $f^{-1}(x)$.
development.solution_text:
Swap each input and output pair $(x, y) \to (y, x)$:
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 3 & 5 & 9 & 15 \\ \hline y & -1 & 0 & 2 & 5 \\ \hline \end{array}$

development.question_text:
The cubic function $f(x) = x^3 - 8$ has an $x$-intercept at $(2, 0)$ and a $y$-intercept at $(0, -8)$.
Determine the intercepts of $y = f^{-1}(x)$.

The function $f(x) = \dfrac{3x - 1}{x + 4}$ has vertical asymptote $x = -4$ and horizontal asymptote $y = 3$.
State the asymptotes and domain of $y = f^{-1}(x)$.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Vertical asymptote of } f^{-1}: x = 3$
$\text{Horizontal asymptote of } f^{-1}: y = -4$
$\text{Domain of } f^{-1}: (-\infty, 3) \cup (3, \infty)$

development.question_text:
The function $f(x) = 3^{x - 1} - 4$ has domain $(-\infty, \infty)$ and range $(-4, \infty)$ with horizontal asymptote $y = -4$.
Find the domain, range, and vertical asymptote of $y = f^{-1}(x)$.
development.solution_text:
$\text{Domain of } f^{-1} = (-4, \infty)$
$\text{Range of } f^{-1} = (-\infty, \infty)$
$\text{Vertical asymptote: } x = -4$

development.question_text:
A line segment on the graph of $y = f(x)$ has endpoints $A(-3, 1)$ and $B(4, 5)$.
Find the endpoints $A'$ and $B'$ of the reflected segment on $y = f^{-1}(x)$ and calculate the midpoint of the reflected segment.

The cubic curve $y = (x - 2)^3 + 1$ has a horizontal point of inflection at $(2, 1)$ and a $y$-intercept at $(0, -7)$.
Find the coordinates of the inflection point and the $x$-intercept of $y = f^{-1}(x)$.

mastery.question_text:
A continuous one-to-one function $f(x)$ has domain $[-4, 6]$ and range $[1, 9]$, with $f(-4) = 1$ and $f(6) = 9$.
State the domain, range, and endpoints of the inverse function $f^{-1}(x)$.

The rational function $f(x) = \dfrac{ax + b}{cx + d}$ with $c \ne 0$ and $ad - bc \ne 0$ has vertical asymptote $x = -\dfrac{d}{c}$ and horizontal asymptote $y = \dfrac{a}{c}$.
Explain why the condition for the asymptotes of $y = f(x)$ to be identical to the asymptotes of $y = f^{-1}(x)$ is $a = -d$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Asymptotes of } f: x = -\dfrac{d}{c}, y = \dfrac{a}{c}$
$\text{Asymptotes of } f^{-1}: x = \dfrac{a}{c}, y = -\dfrac{d}{c}$
$\text{Equating vertical asymptotes: } \dfrac{a}{c} = -\dfrac{d}{c} \implies a = -d$

mastery.question_text:
The tangent to the curve $y = f(x)$ at the point $(2, 8)$ has equation $y = 12x - 16$.
Find the coordinates of the corresponding point on $y = f^{-1}(x)$ and the equation of the tangent line to $y = f^{-1}(x)$ at that point.

A piecewise linear function $y = f(x)$ connects the points $A(-3, -1)$, $B(0, 2)$, and $C(4, 4)$.
Determine the coordinates of the invariant point where $y = f(x)$ meets $y = f^{-1}(x)$ on the line $y = x$.
mastery.solution_text:
$\text{Check given vertices on } y = x: C(4, 4) \text{ has } x = y = 4$
$\text{Invariant point} = (4, 4)$
